with the eastern region of the Iberian Peninsula, with Spain's east coast, the coast over which the sun rises (''levantar'' in Spanish),{{cite web |url=https://www.dictionary.com/browse/levant |title=Levant |publisher=Dictionary.com |access-date=18 September 2018 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304215301/http://dictionary.reference.com/browse/levant |url-status=live }} with the Levant wind that comes from the east, and with the Levante beach in La Malvarrosa where Levante Football Club played some of its earliest fixtures. Levante's earliest games were played at La Platjeta, near the docks on a plot of land owned by a perfume entrepreneur. Its next ground was also near the port area, and the club gradually became associated with the working class. In 1919, the side played Valencia CF for the first time, losing 0–1; the game marked the inauguration of the recently built ground at Algirós. In 1928, Levante FC won its first trophy, the Valencian Championship. 1909 also saw the birth of [[Gimnástico FC|Gimnástico Football Club]], which originally played at Patronato de la Juventud Obrera, being then named Gimnástico-Patronato. In 1919, Gimnástico became the champion of the Campeonato de Valencia, beating CD Castellón in the two-leg finals; the next year, the club became ''Real Gimnástico Football Club'', after being granted royal patronage by [[Alfonso XIII]], and they reached the final of Campeonato Regional de Levante, but lost to Club Deportivo Aguileño. In 1931, with the founding of the [[Second Spanish Republic]], the club dropped the ''Real'' from its name. In [[1934–35 Segunda División|1934–35]], both Levante and Gimnástico debuted in the [[Segunda División|second division]], when the league was expanded from 10 teams to 24. In 1935, Levante won the Campeonato Levante-Sur, a competition that featured teams from [[Valencian Community|Valencia]], Murcia and [[Andalusia]],[https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/span-levantechamp.html Spain – List of Champions of Levante, Valencia and Murcia] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230213165226/https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/span-levantechamp.html |date=13 February 2023 }}; at [[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|RSSSF]] and subsequently reached the semi-finals of the [[Copa del Rey|Spanish Cup]], consecutively beating Valencia and [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] before losing to eventual runners-up [[CE Sabadell FC|Sabadell]]. ===During the civil war: Copa de la España Libre (1937)=== During the [[Spanish Civil War]], Levante and Gimnástico played in the [[Mediterranean League]], finishing fifth and sixth, respectively. Teams from this league also competed in the [[Copa de la España Libre]] ("Free Spain Cup"). It was originally intended that the top four teams from the league would enter the cup, but Barcelona opted to tour Mexico and the United States, and as a result, Levante took its place. The first round of the competition was a mini-league with the top two teams, Levante and Valencia, qualifying for the final. On 18 July 1937, Levante defeated its city rivals 1–0 at the [[Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys|Montjuïc]].[https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spancuplibre37.html Spain – Copa de España Libre 1937]; at RSSSF[https://www.marca.com/futbol/copa-rey/2023/03/25/641ef935ca47410a6f8b4572.html La Federación reconoce la Copa del Levante de 1937 y la del Deportivo de 1912] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230403184710/https://www.marca.com/futbol/copa-rey/2023/03/25/641ef935ca47410a6f8b4572.html |date=3 April 2023 }}, [The Federation recognizes Levante's 1937 Cup and Deportivo's 1912 Cup], Noel Rodilla, Marca, 25 March 2023 (in Spanish) === Merging: Gimnástico and Levante (1939) === [[File:Escut Gimnàtic de València.jpg|thumb|150px|Pennat of [[Gimnástico FC|Gimnàtic de València]] and [[Levante FC]], the two teams that created the Levante UD]] During the Civil War, Levante's ground was destroyed, but the club's squad remained intact. In contrast, Gimnástico had a ground, [[Estadio de Vallejo]], but had lost most of their players. As a result, in 1939 Levante FC and Gimnástico FC merged into Levante Unión Deportiva.{{cite web |url=http://www.levanteud.com/es/historia/anos-20/todo-empezo-en-el-mes-de-septiembre-de-1909 |title=Todo empezó en el mes de septiembre de 1909 |publisher=Levanteud.com |access-date=18 September 2018 |archive-date=20 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180820140924/http://www.levanteud.com/es/historia/anos-20/todo-empezo-en-el-mes-de-septiembre-de-1909 |url-status=dead }} Levante UD can thus trace its origin back to at least 1909 through both Levante FC and Gimnástico FC. The merged club was at first named '''Unión Deportiva Levante-Gimnástico''', then changed it a few years later to '''[[:es:Levante Unión Deportiva|Levante Unión Deportiva]]'''. The current club colours date from this era: the ''blaugrana'', blue-garnet, home colours were originally those of [[Gimnástico FC]], while the black and white away kit were the colours of [[:es:Levante Fútbol Club|Levante FC]]. Levante UD also inherited from Gimnástico FC their nickname, [[wiktionary:granota|''Granota'']], the Frogs.{{cite web|url=https://www.laliga.es/en-GB/news/why-are-levante-called-the-granotas |title=Why are Levante called the 'granotas'? |publisher=Laliga.es |access-date=18 September 2018}}{{cite web |author=La Vanguardia |url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/deportes/20111026/54236143648/las-diez-leyendas-del-levante.html |title=Las diez leyendas del Levante |publisher=Lavanguardia.com |date=26 October 2011 |access-date=18 September 2018 |archive-date=25 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191225032530/https://www.lavanguardia.com/deportes/20111026/54236143648/las-diez-leyendas-del-levante.html |url-status=live }}{{Cite web|url=https://www.levante-emv.com/deportes/2009/08/31/levante-cumple-cien-anos/626049.html|title=El Levante cumple cien años... Más dos|date=31 August 2009|access-date=15 August 2018|archive-date=23 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180623193815/https://www.levante-emv.com/deportes/2009/08/31/levante-cumple-cien-anos/626049.html|url-status=live}} === La Liga: relegations and promotions (1963–present) === Levante had to wait until the 1960s to make its [[La Liga]] debut. In 1963, the club finished runner-up in Group II of the second division, defeating [[Deportivo de La Coruña]] 4–2 on aggregate in the promotion play-offs. During [[1963–64 La Liga|the first top flight season]], it managed to win both games against Valencia, and also achieved a 5–1 home win against Barcelona in [[1964–65 La Liga|the 1964–65 campaign]], but was relegated nonetheless after losing in the playoffs against [[CD Málaga|Málaga]]. It spent most of the following two decades in the second and [[Tercera División|third divisions]]; the [[Segunda División B]] would not be created until 1977. [[File:Cruyff levante vs palencia.jpg|thumb|170px|left|[[Johan Cruyff]] on his debut with Levante, March 1981]] In the early 1980s, Dutch superstar [[Johan Cruyff]] played half a season for the club, retiring three years later. After winning [[2003–04 Segunda División|2003–04's second division]], Levante returned to the top level but survived only [[2004–05 La Liga|one season]]. Finishing third in [[2005–06 Segunda División|2005–06]], it returned for two additional campaigns, the decisive match in the [[2006–07 La Liga|2006–07 season]] being a 4–2 home win against Valencia courtesy of [[Riga Mustapha]] (two goals), [[Salva Ballesta|Salva]] and [[Laurent Courtois]]. Levante's financial status worsened, however, and there were reports that the players had only received approximately one-fifth of their contractual payments. News reports stated that the club had incurred a debt of over €18 million in payments due to its players. The team plummeted down the standings, and it was confirmed with several matches to go that the club would be playing in the second division in [[2008–09 Segunda División|2008–09]]. The players protested at their lack of payments at one point, refusing to move for several seconds after the opening whistle against Deportivo and later announcing that they would [[Strike action|strike]] during the [[2007–08 La Liga|season]]-ending game at [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]]. The threat was withdrawn when league officials announced that a benefit game would be played between a Levante XI and a Primera División XI, with all receipts going to pay the Levante players' wages. On 13 June 2010, Levante returned to La Liga after a 3–1 home win against [[2009–10 Segunda División|already relegated]] [[CD Castellón|Castellón]], making its final round 0–4 defeat at [[Real Betis]] irrelevant.[https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2011/oct/31/la-liga-levante-finally-dethroned Levante are finally dethroned as La Liga becomes a more boring place] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240614155738/https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2011/oct/31/la-liga-levante-finally-dethroned |date=14 June 2024 }}; ''[[The Guardian]]'', 31 October 2011 Under the manager who led the team back to the top flight, [[Luis García Plaza]], Levante finally retained its top division status in the [[2010–11 La Liga|2010–11 season]]. At one point in the league's second round of matches, Levante was third in the table behind Barcelona and Real Madrid, after losing just once (against Real Madrid) in 12 games.[https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2011/oct/17/levante-la-liga-expendables-2 Levante are back and this time they're ready to take on the world] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240614155754/https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2011/oct/17/levante-la-liga-expendables-2 |date=14 June 2024 }}; ''The Guardian'', 17 October 2011 [[File:Levante Unión Deportiva league performance 1929-present.svg|thumb|Chart of Levante UD league performance 1929–present]] On 26 October 2011, during round nine of [[2011–12 La Liga|the season]], Levante defeated [[Real Sociedad]] 3–2 to move top of the first division table for the first time in the club's history, with 23 points.[http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/writers/sid_lowe/10/26/levante/index.html Levante pulls off the impossible] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111028223327/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/writers/sid_lowe/10/26/levante/index.html |date=28 October 2011 }}; [[Sports Illustrated]], 26 October 2011 In the process, it recorded seven straight wins after drawing its first two games.[https://www.nytimes.com/2011/10/29/sports/soccer/levante-la-ligas-david-stares-down-at-spains-two-goliaths.html Underdog turns heads at the top in Spain] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161223064144/http://www.nytimes.com/2011/10/29/sports/soccer/levante-la-ligas-david-stares-down-at-spains-two-goliaths.html |date=23 December 2016 }}; ''[[The New York Times]]'', 28 October 2011 The club eventually finished sixth after defeating [[Athletic Bilbao]] 3–0 at home in its last match, thus [[2012–13 UEFA Europa League|qualifying]] for the [[UEFA Europa League]] for the first time in its history.{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/323688/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5739|title=Ghezzal helps Levante secure European place|publisher=[[ESPN Soccernet]]|date=13 May 2012|access-date=27 October 2013|archive-date=23 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131223233925/http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/323688/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5739|url-status=live}} There, they made it to the last 16 before a 2–0 extra-time loss to Russia's [[FC Rubin Kazan]].{{cite news |title=Rubin edge out Levante in extra time |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0207-0e9f041fff58-abfc52c75a5d-1000--rubin-edge-out-levante-in-extra-time/ |access-date=16 June 2020 |publisher=UEFA |date=14 March 2013 |archive-date=16 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200616165830/https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0207-0e9f041fff58-abfc52c75a5d-1000--rubin-edge-out-levante-in-extra-time/ |url-status=live }} [[File:Deportivolevante.JPG|thumb|300px|[[Deportivo de La Coruña]] vs. Levante.]] In the [[2015-16 La Liga|2015–16 season]], Levante was relegated after defeat by [[Málaga CF|Málaga]] and finished last. The club was promoted back to the top league in [[2016–17 Segunda División|2016–17]], winning the [[Segunda División]] title. In the [[2017-18 La Liga|2017–18 season]], the club secured safety in the league and on 13 May, beat the champions [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] 5–4 (having led 5–1 early in the second half), with [[Emmanuel Boateng (footballer, born 1996)|Emmanuel Boateng]] scoring his first ever career hat-trick.{{Cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/en/football/barcelona/2018/05/13/5af89e9a268e3e46378b460f.html|title=LaLiga – Levante 5–4 Barcelona: Emmanuel Boateng scores the first hat-trick of his career against Barcelona|work=MARCA in English|access-date=14 May 2018|archive-date=2 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180702122231/http://www.marca.com/en/football/barcelona/2018/05/13/5af89e9a268e3e46378b460f.html|url-status=live}} This win ended Barcelona's hopes of achieving an unbeaten season.{{cite news |last1=Grounds |first1=Ben |title=Levante 5-4 Barcelona: Catalans' unbeaten run comes to an end in nine-goal thriller |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11827/11371805/levante-5-4-barcelona-catalans-unbeaten-run-comes-to-an-end |access-date=31 August 2020 |work=Sky Sports |date=14 May 2018 |archive-date=23 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180823114107/http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11827/11371805/levante-5-4-barcelona-catalans-unbeaten-run-comes-to-an-end |url-status=live }} In the [[2021-22 La Liga|2021–22 season]], Levante was relegated after being defeated 0–6 by Real Madrid, ending their five years in the top tier. == Seasons == ===Recent history=== [[File:Levante (2013).jpg|thumbnail|Before a game in March 2013]] {|class="wikitable" |- style="background:#efefef;" !
